{{nihongo|'''Suzu Shrine'''|須須神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Suzu, Ishikawa|ar|سوزو (إيشيكاوا)|azb|سوزو، ایشیکاوا|ce|Судзу|ceb|Suzu (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Suzu (Išikawa)|de|Suzu (Ishikawa)|es|Suzu|et|Suzu|fa|سوزو، ایشیکاوا|fi|Suzu|fr|Suzu|gl|Suzu|id|Suzu, Ishikawa|it|Suzu|ja|珠洲市|ko|스즈시|ms|Suzu, Ishikawa|mzn|سوزو، ایشیکاوا|nl|Suzu|pl|Suzu (miasto)|pt|Suzu|ro|Suzu|ru|Судзу|sv|Suzu|tg|Сузу|th|ซูซุ|tl|Suzu|tr|Suzu|tt|Судзу|uk|Судзу|ur|سوزو، اشیکاوا|vi|Suzu, Ishikawa|war|Suzu, Ishikawa|zh|珠洲市|zh_classical|珠洲市|zh_min_nan|Suzu-chhī|zh_yue|珠洲|qid=Q846345}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|Q131281|qid=Q131281}}. '''Takakura-gu''' and '''Kinbun-gu''' are in {{ill|Misaki|ja|三崎村 (石川県)|ko|미사키촌 (이시카와현)|qid=Q11355314|lt=Misaki-cho Jike}}, Suzu<ref name="ishikawa-jinjacho" />, and the '''Okumiya''' is in Noro-machi, Suzu<ref name="ishikawa-jinjacho_okumiya" />. {{nihongo|'''Suzu Shrine'''|須須神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Noto Province]].

== Overview ==
It is located in the northeastern part of Suzu City. The enshrined deities are {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Amatsu-Hitaka-Hiko-Ho-no-Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}, Miho Susumi-no-Mikoto, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|az|Konohanasakuya|ca|Konohana no Sakuya hime|de|Konohanasakuyahime|fa|کونوهاناساکویا-هیمه|fr|Konohana-no-Sakuya|it|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|コノハナノサクヤビメ|ko|고노하나노사쿠야비메|mni|ꯀꯣꯅꯣꯍꯅꯁꯀꯨꯌ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Konohanasakuya-hime|ru|Коноханасакуя-химэ|sv|Konohanasakuyahime|th|เซ็นเง็ง|vi|Konohana Sakuya Hime|zh|木花開耶姬|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto}}, and three others. Near Takakura-gu are Suzu Shrine Okumiya and Suzu Shrine Kinbun-gu.

It holds cultural properties including a wooden male deity statue designated as a national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}. On {{ill|April 24|Q2529|qid=Q2529}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 27), it was certified as a {{ill|Japan Heritage|Q18382798|qid=Q18382798}} component under "Lanterns Dancing on the Peninsula: Noto - Enthralling Kiriko Festivals."

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as a small government-offering shrine. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was ranked as a prefectural shrine.

There are three torii in the precinct, but in the {{ill|2023|Q49622|qid=Q49622}} Okunoto earthquake of May, the first torii (about 9 m tall) collapsed and removal work began in August<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Removal begins at public expense for collapsed torii at Suzu Shrine|url=https://www.hokkoku.co.jp/articles/-/1155732 |website=Hokkoku Shimbun |date=2023-08-18 |access-date=2023-08-18 |language=ja}}</ref><ref name="nikkansports20240121" />.
In the {{ill|2024|Q49619|qid=Q49619}} {{ill|2024 Noto earthquake|Q124060919|qid=Q124060919|lt=Noto Peninsula earthquake}}, the second torii collapsed due to quake and tsunami effects, and the third torii developed cracks<ref name="nikkansports20240121">{{Cite web |title=Suzu's Suzu Shrine heavily damaged again after last year; assistant priest Toyonobu Sarume: "Only rebuilding remains"|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/general/nikkan/news/202401210000971.html |website=Nikkan Sports|date=2024-01-21 |access-date=2024-01-21 |language=ja}}</ref>. In the same quake, the temizuya was completely destroyed, doors of the main hall were warped, and stone lanterns and guardian dogs were also damaged<ref name="nikkansports20240121" />.

== Access ==
* By car
: From {{ill|Noto-Satoyama Kaidō|Q11612031|qid=Q11612031}}{{ill|Anamizu Interchange|Q11597233|qid=Q11597233|lt=Anamizu I.C.}}, go east via {{ill|Suzu Road|Q11573344|qid=Q11573344}}, then from the Rice Center-mae intersection take Prefectural Route 287 for about 1 hour.
* Public transport
: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Suzu Bus}}, Noro-Iida (sea) route bound for "Noro," get off at "Suzu Jinja-mae"<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.suzu.lg.jp/site/kankou/1530.html |title=Suzu Shrine |publisher=Suzu City |date=2022-01-17 |accessdate=2024-01-12 }}</ref>.
